docs.title: Gacha, Summons & Economy
docs.text:
Is there a Tier List?

This game is roster-based, not team-based; thus there is no reliable Tier List since you tend to use different characters depending on the situation. Anything you see online can have some degree of truth, but it still wouldn't capture the whole complexity of the game.

The only thing that stays correct all the time:Supports are the highest priority since you use them constantly, unlike DPS.

How do I get Characters? How does the costume system work?

You can think of Costumes as Skills of a Character.

Whenever you obtain the first costume of the Character, they are unlocked automatically. You do not need to pull for Characters.

Who should I pull for?

Refer to Banner Recommendations.

Alternatively, as a new player, you can spend some amount of pulls into 12-Pick Selective Banner, prioritizing Supports.

View 12-Pick Recommendations →

Who do I get from the Newbie Infinite Draw?

The best Costume to get from there is The Curse Celia.

She is a late-game oriented pick, so you should not expect immediate benefit from her. Nonetheless, she is an important Chainer to have.

Do not worry about any weapons or other costumes; it is not worth the time spent on rerolling the banner.

How does the Selective Draw work? Is 1-Pick or 12-Pick better?

Selective Draw (Banners) work in a way that you pick desired Costumes and they have increased chances to appear. They are the only banners that accept Selective Draw Tickets.

Essentially, Selective Draw is displayed in the form of 12-Pick (Permanent) and 1-Pick (recurring) Banners.

As a new player, 12-Pick is objectively better.

View 12-Pick Recommendations →

Who should I put in 12-Pick?

Generally speaking, Supports. These include not just Buffers, but Chainers and Amplifiers.

If you're completely new, you can set the following Costumes:

  • Queen of Gluttis Granadair ( Water) (until +5)
  • Shrine Maiden of Purification Granadair ( Water) (until +5)
  • Water Park Queen Wilhelmina ( Water) (until +4)
  • Homunculus Lathel ( Fire) (until +5)
  • Dark Saintess Liberta ( Fire) (until +5)
  • Onsen Manager Liberta ( Fire) (until +5)
  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana ( Wind) (until +5)
  • Magical Innovator Diana ( Wind) (until +0)
  • Robin Hood Zenith ( Wind) (until +3 or +5)
  • B-Rank Idol Helena ( Light) (until +5)
  • Pure White Blessing Refithea ( Light) (until +1 or +5)
  • Poolside Fairy Refithea ( Light) (until +3 or +5)

Keep in mind that for Dark Saintess Liberta and Adventurer of the Unknown Diana, there is a Pub Recruitment; thus, if you haven't recruited them yet, remove at +4 instead.

Visual Costume Display

If you need a replacement for some of the costumes listed above due to completion, pick the following:

  • Poolside Guardian Zenith ( Wind) (until +5)
  • Iron Monarch Wilhelmina ( Water) (until +4)
  • Sunny Inn Hand Helena ( Light) (until +5)
  • Red Riding Hood Rou ( Darkness) (until +5)
  • Young Lady Blade ( Darkness) (until +5)
  • Medical Club Teresse ( Water) (until +5)
  • Shadowed Dream Sonya ( Darkness) (until +4 or +5)
  • Miracle Marine Mamonir ( Water) (until +5)
  • Heavenly Guardian Successor Glacia ( Water) (until +4)
  • New Hire Seir ( Darkness) (until +5)
  • Shadowed Bunny Eleaneer ( Darkness) (until +4)

By the time you need more replacements, better to ask for personal advice in the Discord Server.

Who to pick from Recommended ★5 Costume Selective Ticket?

Generally, it depends on who you have from those tickets beforehand.

Assuming you have no one, you should pick

  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana +2 (3 tickets)
  • B-Rank Idol Helena +1 (2 tickets)
  • Homunculus Lathel +2 (3 tickets)
  • New Hire Seir +0 (1 ticket)
  • Track and Field Captain Levia +0 (1 ticket)
  • Robin Hood Zenith +0 (1 ticket)
  • Game Club Rafina +0 (1 ticket)

Assuming you also bought Mega SALE!!! First Time Countdown Package!, your choice changes to:

  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana +4 (5 tickets)
  • B-Rank Idol Helena +3 (4 tickets)
  • Homunculus Lathel +3 (4 tickets)
  • ...

Order, generally speaking, does not matter since at the end you will have the same costume set either way. Nonetheless, you can start by picking B-Rank Idol Helena +1 first to comfortably run your starting team.

If you are not sure, it is always better to ask in a Discord Server.

How do Property Tickets work? Who do I pick?

Property Selective Draw Exchange Ticket allows you to choose a Property and receive a random ★5 Costume from the chosen Property.

As a new player, almost every Property is good to spend tickets on. You can focus on Light until you get decent Refithea. Later on, you can do the math to see what gives more useful Costumes on average. Even later on, you can do the math to see what gives less Threads on average due to owning a lot of +5 Costumes.

How to get more Tickets and Diamonds?
  • Using Coupon Codes
  • Completing Evil Castle
  • Completing Character Packs
  • Completing Event Packs
  • Collecting Chests in Battle Zones in Packs
  • Reaching Lvl 10 in Fiend Hunter
  • Event Shop
  • Guild Shop
  • Guide / Season Passes
  • Achievements

And, honestly, just playing the game.

Who to recruit from the pub?

Highest priority is taken by Supports:

  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana — Story Pack 10 (Homunculus)
  • Dark Saintess Liberta — Story Pack 15 (Promise of Vengeance)
  • Queen of Gluttis Granadair — Random Appearance
  • Any Costume that appears in a Pub and has Active Banner
  • Night of Death Mamonir — Random Appearance
  • Fiend Scholar Olstein — Story Pack 4 (Cat Daddy) [if you do not have any other Costume]
  • Swadowed Dream Palette — Story Pack 20 (Into the Abyss)
  • The Gluttonous Refithea — Random Appearance
  • The Curse Celia — Random Appearance

The remaining Costumes are either DPS or Low Priority / Niche picks. It's up to you what to follow afterwards. Alternatively, ask in a Discord Server.

docs.title: Battle & Mechanics
docs.text:
What is 'Property' and how does it work?

Property is technically the Element of each Character.

There are a lotal of 6 Properties: Water, Fire, Wind, Light, Darkness and Neutral.

  • Water Allies deal more damage to Fire Enemies and less damage to Wind Enemies
  • Fire Allies deal more damage to Wind Enemies and less damage to Water Enemies
  • Wind Allies deal more damage to Water Enemies and less damage to Fire Enemies
  • Light Allies deal more damage to Darkness Enemies
  • Darkness Allies deal more damage to Light Enemies

Neutral Property cannot receive more or less damage from any other Property.

Increased damage can be influenced by Property Buffs.

How to build a good team?

A good (general content) team:

  • Uses only one type of damage, Physical or Magical (unless you absolutely know what you are doing and can explain every single moment regarding your decision)
  • Uses both Supports (usually 3, can be two) and DPS
  • Has a correct order of Costumes (Supports first, DPS second)
  • Does NOT use Property Buffs whenever the team is at no gain from it
  • Focuses either on Large AoE Damage (for regular fights) or Single Target Nuke Damage (for Solo Boss fights)
  • Uses different Buff Types whenever it is possible (Augmentation / Vulnerability, ATK Buff etc).
  • Is built around finishing the battle on Turn 1, or, at max, on Turn 3
  • Can activate all abilities on Turn 1, or, in other words, has enough SP
  • Has the best Gear you have at the moment

For Single Target Bosses, the easiest solution (in most cases) is a Physical team with Zenith and Ventana as your main DPS, which you can borrow from friends.

docs.title: Upgrades & Progression
docs.text:
Who do I level/upgrade first?

You need to be careful when using the upgrade term, since it can be applied to a lot of Costumes' / Characters' aspects.

  • When it comes down to Level, prefer using Slimes for your DPS
  • When it comes down to Potential Liberation, focus on Supports first. More about Potential Liberation →
  • When it comes down to Gear, prioritize DPS. More about Gear System →
  • When it comes down to Engraving / Awakening, it is used on DPS, but it is very expensive for a new player, so hold onto resources.
    • If you do this for Guide Pass Task, Awakening Nebris is one of the best choices
  • When it comes down to Burst, there is no definitive answer since the mechanic is new. However, the Author suggests focusing on Supports, similar to Potential Liberation More about Burst System →
  • When it comes down to Costume copies, generally Supports are preferred; however, there may be exceptions. Refer to Banner Recommendations in case you are hesitating.
What gear should I craft?

Refer to the Crafting Guide.

More about Gear System →

Who to spend Tears of Goddess and Crystals on?

Refer to the Cymmina's Guide.

More about Potential Liberation →

Who to spend Sparkles of Rampage on?

Since this is a relatively new feature, there is no one united opinion on this topic.

You can refer to Priority Guide from the Author of the site, but definitely read General Advice and Disclaimer before you do that.

More about Burst System →

Should I Engrave / Awaken someone? Who to Engrave / Awaken?

As was stated in the "Who do I level/upgrade first?" question, engraving is not worth it for new players. This is an expensive procedure that does not give much benefit.

Nonetheless, if you decided to Engrave / Awaken someone, it should be the DPS you use the most, such as Nebris.

How can I play the game on PC?

You can download the client using this link.

My characters appear to be black(ened). How do I fix it?

This happens because Silhouette Mode is enabled. It uses silhouettes instead of sprites and disables animations.

To remove it, head to Settings → Graphics → Silhouette Mode → Disable.

Image Guide

Is there censorship in this game?
  • One active form of censorship is for German citizens. There, a few game sprites have altered appearance, as well as some Ability cutscenes, Medical Club Teresse Fated Guest, and Slap Pop Pop! Minigame were removed.
  • Another active form of censorship is for Korean citizens, where Shattered Dream Palette and Retired Legend Olivier cutscenes were modified, as well as Retired Legend Olivier Fated Guest was modified as well.
  • The game is not legally accessible in Vietnam and Netherlands, but there are workarounds to download the game from there.
How to display my own collection when asking for a team build?
  • When asking for a team, use Last Night to show the Costumes you have. To do that,
    1. Go to the Last Night Pack and walk towards the battle area
    2. Tap Replace → Replace → Reset → Confirm.
    3. Click the second icon in the top right corner and sort "By Deployed First ↓" and screenshot your costumes.
Image Guide

  • When asking for an Awakening / Potential Liberation / Burst help, use Companion tab with View Costume button enabled.
Image Guide

  • When asking for a help with Gear, use second menu inside of Companion tab. It captures the gear for your main team (which is usually the best) and some extra gear on the right side. Later on, you can show from the bag by using Custom Marks and filtering to display them first.

docs.title: New Player Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to Brown Dust 2! Whether you are starting fresh or returning after a break, navigating the game's cartridge system, gacha mechanics, and tactical grid battles can feel overwhelming at first.

This guide provides a structured roadmap to help you build an efficient account from Day 1 without wasting scarce resources. Below you will find breakdowns of the interface, early battle solutions, gacha and ticket priorities, core team templates, and essential daily farming routines.

If you are looking for quick navigation:

  • Clear Master Pack 1 (Edge of Dimensions) to unlock the gacha and core event hubs.
  • Target The Curse Celia in the Infinite Draw and save your Selective Tickets for meta supports (mostly Adventurer of the Unknown Diana, B-Rank Idol Helena, Homunculus Lathel).
  • Never mix Physical and Magic buffers and DPS in the same team composition.

docs.title: Field Menu Layout
docs.text:
Field Menu Layout

1 — Minimap & Map Info (Top-Left)
  • Collection & Rapport & Other Bonuses — View active global stat bonuses applied to the current Pack.
  • Minimap & Enlarging Button ([+] Icon) — Shows immediate surroundings; tap the [+] icon to expand into the bigger version of itself, tap the minimap directly to expand into the full area map.
  • Shortcut Menu — Fast-travel to key landmarks, such as the Inn or Hunting Grounds.
  • Rewards & Exploration Info — Tracks remaining collectibles (glimmers), search objects, and field monsters left in the area.
  • Health Bar & Food Option — Track HP of the first Character and enable restoring HP with Food.
2 — Resources, Shortcuts & Quests (Top-Right)
  • Current Currencies — Displays current totals for Dia, Gold, and Ability Pills.
  • Companion — Manage your character roster: level up, equip costumes, upgrade gear, allocate Potential Liberation nodes, Awakening and Burst upgrades.
  • Bag — View your inventory of consumables, gear and collection.
  • Home — Return directly to the Home Screen.
  • Quest Tracker — Displays active quest goals. Tap the tracker to activate Auto-Move pathfinding, or tap the [+] icon to view full quest details.
3 — Interaction, Field Abilities & Movement (Bottom-Right)
  • Interaction Button — Interact with objects on the map.
  • Field Abilities Shortcut — Quick-cast equipped Field Abilities (Search, Absorption, Assemble, Overpower, Danger Detection etc.) using Ability Pills.
  • Dash — Sprint to move faster in fast motion.
  • Field Abilities Presets — Cycle between 3 customizable sets of assigned Field Abilities.
4 — Miscellaneous (Bottom)
  • Pack Selection (Cartridges) — Switch between Main Story Packs, Character Packs, and Special Content Packs (e.g., Evil Castle, Mirror Wars).
  • Field Character — Toggle field sprite appearance between the Story Team, Custom Character, or active Battle Team.
  • Field Ability Menu — Use Field Abilities of Characters or create a Shortcut / Presets.

Each Character can use only 1 Costume (Skill) per turn.

docs.title: Home Screen Layout
docs.text:
Home Screen Layout

1 — Social & Daily Management (Top-Left)
  • Profile / Account — View player Profile & Combat Power. Tapping the plus icon displays your Player ID and detailed account statistics.
  • My Room — Customize and decorate a personal dormitory that can be visited by other players.
  • Friends — Manage your friend list and set your shared Support Character.
  • Guild — Access daily Guild check-ins and participate in seasonal Guild Raids.
  • Business Management — Quick-claim shortcuts for passive resource generation from Glupy Diner, Fishing Voyage, and Territory Helpers.
  • GluTalk — Text message conversations with specific Costumes to obtain special wallpapers and interactions (Secret Events).
  • Rapport — Deepen affinity with specific Costumes / Characters via gifts / dialogue to earn permanent global stat buffs and Dia.
  • Arcade — Access standalone mini-games.
  • Secret Events / View Mode — Trigger special interactive cutscenes with specific Costumes, or hide the UI for a clean background view.
2 — Currencies, System & Shortcuts (Top-Right)
  • Current Currencies — Displays current totals for Dia, Gold, and Ability Pills.
  • Notices — Official patch notes, maintenance alerts, update announcements, and player feedback surveys.
  • Mailbox — Collect login bonuses, maintenance compensation, package purchases, pass and coupon codes rewards.
  • Wallpaper Editor — Customize lobby artwork.
  • Settings & ETC (Grid Icon) — Account linking/switching, settings, customer support, and the official in-game Guidebook.
  • News Ticker — Scrolling banner alerting you of banners or events ending soon.
  • Return Season — Special event button that appears during Fiend Hunter rerun seasons.
  • Tactical Manual — Shortcut to Taros Tactical Manual, a monthly tactical puzzle mode with clearance rewards.
  • Pass — Central hub for the Guide Pass, Season Pass, Character Pass and other seasonal passes.
  • Quick Hunt — Instantly sweep unlocked Hunting Grounds and Path of Adventure stages without having to load into the map.
3 — Cartridges & Event Shortcuts (Bottom-Right)
  • Prestige & Special Skins — View active cosmetic skins offers (purely visual overhauls with no gameplay stat bonuses).
  • Season Event — Shortcut to the current limited-time event hub (Event Story, Mini-game, Fiend Hunter, and Event Shop).
  • Pack Selection (Cartridges) — Switch between Main Story Packs, Character Packs, and Special Content Packs (e.g., Evil Castle, Mirror Wars).

You Need to Know This

Season Event button is scrollable. Doing so will give you the access to the previous Seasonal Event Shop, allowing you to spend the currency.

More about Season Event Shop →

4 — Navigation Dock (Bottom)
  • Jukebox — Select background music from the unlocked soundtrack collection.
  • Draw (Gacha) — Summon on rate-up banners, standard banners, and claim daily free pulls.
  • Companion — Manage your character roster: level up, equip costumes, upgrade gear, allocate Potential Liberation nodes, Awakening and Burst upgrades.
  • Bag — View your inventory of consumables, gear and collection.
  • Story (Archive) — Story replay archive for main story chapters, seasonal events, and cutscenes. (Note: Reading stories here does not progress the actual game).
  • Collection — Track collected costumes, weapons and items to get permanent account-wide Collection stat bonuses.
  • Missions — Track Daily and Weekly tasks for regular Dia and other resources income.
  • Achv (Achievements) — Long-term account milestones, trophy achievements, and title rewards.
  • Event — Special check-ins, Pickup Missions and ongoing reward campaigns.
  • Shop — In-game exchange shops using earned gameplay currencies (Golden Thread, Mirror Wars medals, Powder of Hope).
  • Premium Shop — Cash shop for Dia bundles, subscription packs, and special paid packages.

docs.title: Recommended ★5 Costume Selective Tickets
docs.text:
Recommended ★5 Costume Selective Tickets are the ones that are given as a reward in a Guide Pass, as well as some Paid Packages.

Each Ticket allows you to pick 1 Costume amongst 12 suggested.

To use tickets, head to the bag and press corresponding button.

Image Guide

Selection Menu

Guide Pass gives you 12 tickets. Mega SALE!!! First Time Countdown Package! (Paid Package) gives another 5. Occasional other Paid Packages can give you 3 tickets as well.

Assuming you have no one, you should pick

  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana +2 (3 tickets)
  • B-Rank Idol Helena +1 (2 tickets)
  • Homunculus Lathel +2 (3 tickets)
  • New Hire Seir +0 (1 ticket)
  • Track and Field Captain Levia +0 (1 ticket)
  • Robin Hood Zenith +0 (1 ticket)
  • Game Club Rafina +0 (1 ticket)

Assuming you also bought Mega SALE!!! First Time Countdown Package!, your choice changes to:

  • Adventurer of the Unknown Diana +4 (5 tickets)
  • B-Rank Idol Helena +3 (4 tickets)
  • Homunculus Lathel +3 (4 tickets)
  • ...

Order, generally speaking, does not matter since at the end you will have the same costume set either way. Nonetheless, you can start by picking B-Rank Idol Helena +1 first to comfortably run your starting team.

docs.title: Infinite Draw
docs.text:
Infinite Draw is a banner that allows you to obtain free ★5 Costume within some pool. You can roll the banner infinitely, but keep in mind that only 1 ★5 Costume is possible from it.

As soon as you claim your draw, you will have the access to the rest active banners.

For the Infinite Draw, go for The Curse Celia Costume. Rest, such as Gear or ★4 Costumes, does not matter.

Nowadays, there are some other viable choices like Gentle Maid Anastasia and Top Idol Helena, but since game is support-heavy, Celia is still recommended over DPS or defensive Supports.

docs.title: Teams
docs.text:
Generally speaking, there is no universal team for every content. Broadly, it depends on enemies.

However, for simplification, in a story you tend to run the same core stuff with some modifications.

The general idea is 1-3 DPS, with rest being Supports. 3 Supports and 2 DPS is author's preferred team composition for simple fights, although it can vary.

Avoid Mixing Physical & Magic Damage Types!

Keep your buffers and DPS within same damage type, unless you know what you are doing.

  • ATK Buffers (Arines, Homunculus Lathel) only buff Physical damage.
  • MATK Buffers (B-Rank Idol Helena, Elpis) only buff Magical damage.
  • Universal Buffers (Kind Student Samay, Adventurer of the Unknown Diana) buff both damage types.

docs.title: General Content AoE Team
docs.text:
This team is designed to clear battle with a lot of enemies.

Newbie AoE Team

Text Version
  • Slot 1 — B-Rank Idol Helena — 5★ Support — from Recommended ★5 Costume Selective Ticket.
  • Slot 2 — Hand of Salvation Elpis — 4★ Support — from any Gacha banner.
  • Slot 3 — Kind Student Samay — 4★ Support — from any Gacha banner.
    • Substitute — Queen of Gluttis Granadair — 5★ Support — from random Pub Recruit.
    • Substitute — Adventurer of the Unknown Diana — 5★ Support — from Story Pack 10 Pub Recruit — if enemy is Light or Fire.
  • Slot 4 — Dream Bride Eclipse — 5★ DPS — from Events Tab.
  • Slot 5 — Summer Vacation Dalvi — 5★ DPS — from Events Tab.

Costumes vs Characters

To clarify things, in a battle you use Characters.

On the image and in the list, Costumes are provided as a Turn 1 option. If you use these Costumes (Skills) on Turn 1, you have more chances to finish the battle in a single turn.

Do I really have to use ★3/4 Characters?

There is absolutely nothing wrong with using ★3/4 Supports. To be even more precise, ★5 equivalents are often worse at low upgrade dupes than +5 ★3/4 Costumes.

Of course, you can replace them once you are established in the game, but it should not be your main objective early on.

What positioning should I use?

There is no solid concrete positioning, because it varies based on the enemies.

If your current positioning clears, there is no reason to change it. If you fail, check positioning first.

Nonetheless, most of layouts vulnerable to damage from middle row/column, therefore, put DPS in the middle, while supports positioning does not matter much.

One of possible positioning layouts

Additional Note

Dalvi's and Eclipse's order can be altered based on enemies. Supports order in this team does not matter.

  • Slot 4 — Kind Student Samay — 4★ Support — from any Gacha banner.
    • Substitute — Adventurer of the Unknown Diana — 5★ Support — from Story Pack 10 Pub Recruit — if enemy is Darkness.
    • Substitute — The Curse Celia — 5★ Support — from Infinite Draw Gacha Banner.

How to Borrow?

  1. Find a person with the unit you need, either via social media, in-game or via other means.
  2. Send request and get accepted.
  3. Head into the battle, then press Replace → Hand symbol in the top right corner → Pick the desired unit.

docs.title: Hunting Grounds, Path of Adventure & Quick Hunt
docs.text:
Quick Hunt you can see on the Home Screen and Field Screen is combined menu for Hunting Grounds and Path of Adventure.

Quick Hunt Menu

It serves as a shortcut, in which you do not have to manually do 6 fights in order to clear a dungeon. Yet, all unlock requirements remain the same:

  • Story Pack 3 Cleared for Goblin Cave, Slime Empire and Magic Crystal Caves
  • Story Pack 1 — 10 Normal Difficulty Cleared for Hunting Grounds 1 — 10 correspondingly.

How should I use Rice and Torches?

Gear have different Rarity ( — ), Tier (I — IV), Upgrade Level (+1 — +9), and Refinement Score (6 — 24). The higher the number everywhere, the better.

To craft Gear, you need to upgrade the Crafting Ability first (Fred / Layla). To do that, you need to earn EXP and then update it. The EXP required is equivalent to at most 20-40 crafts of gear for each level.

docs.title: Season Events
docs.text:
A Season Event is a recurring, limited-time activity typically lasting two weeks that introduces unique story content, specialized combat encounters, and event-exclusive rewards.

To access the event, find the icon on the right side of the Home Screen.

Image Guide

docs.title: Event Menu
docs.text:
Event Menu

The Event Menu typically consists of:

  • Story
  • Normal Battles
  • Challenge Battles
  • Minigame (rarely)
  • Fiend Hunter
  • Missions
  • Event Shop
  • Event Costumes List

docs.title: Story
docs.text:
The Story of the Season Event is a Rapport Story of the specific Costume. It consists of 6 Episodes, with each Episode giving Event Currency (650 for the first 5 Episodes and 750 for the last Episode).

Story Menu

Learn More about Rapport Story →

Before the Rapport update, each Story was usually split between 2 Season Events. It meant that typically half of the story was given in the first two weeks (first Season Event), and the other half of the story was given in the second two weeks (second Season Event).

Stories from previous Events

You can read old Stories via the Story tab from the main menu, but you will not receive any rewards from doing so. Rapport Stories do not appear there, since they will get locked behind Rapport Level once the Season Event ends.

  • Currently, Going Home and Operation M.O.E. Season Events are not available due to certain circumstances; you can find records of those on YouTube.
Image Guide

Note that Stories take the name of the Event of the first two weeks (if they are combined).

That means that the whole story covered in both «Strange Request» and «Dark Magica» Season Events is displayed under the «Strange Request» name.

docs.title: Event Costume
docs.text:
In each Event, there are a total of 4 Costumes that are chosen to be the Event ones.

You can check the list of Costumes by pressing the corresponding tab at the top of the page.

Image Guide

Event Costume Tab Display

Each Costume provides a Bonus to the Event Currency Gain from Normal and Challenge Battles, up to 100%.

To obtain a bonus, you only need to own the costumes, not use them in the battle.

docs.title: Normal and Challenge Battles
docs.text:
In each Event, there is a total of 15 Normal and Challenge Battles you can participate in.

Successfully winning any Battle gives you Event Currency and removes 1 daily attempt. Additionally, there are 3 Clear Rewards — one-time rewards obtained whenever you satisfy the condition.

Conditions

  • Win the Battle
  • Win with everyone survived[1] / Win the battle with less than 2 fatigued[2]
  • Win the battle within 8 turns or less

[1]: For Normal Battles 1-4, 5-9 and 11-14. [2]: For Normal Battles 5, 10, 15 and all Challenge Battles.

The Clear Rewards do not change depending on the Level and are affected only by the type of Battle (Normal / Challenge) and Event Currency Boost Gain.

Clear Rewards

Normal Battles:

  • 250 Event Currency
  • 25 Dias
  • 25 Dias

Challenge Battles:

  • 250 Event Currency
  • 50K Gold
  • 50K Gold

Event Currency Boost Gain is applied after the battle victory, meaning, with full bonus (100%), you will receive 500 despite 250 being displayed.

docs.title: Daily Attempts
docs.text:
As was stated above, each successful clear uses 1 Attempt (Attempt Point). If you fail or restart the battle, no attempts are consumed, meaning you can experiment as much as you want.

Each day, you have 5 Attempts. They are refreshed daily at 00:00 UTC. That means that for the whole duration of the event, you have 70 free attempts.

docs.title: Repeating Battles
docs.text:
If you are stuck at one particular battle or have won them all, you can retry the completed battle to obtain Repeat Reward.

The Repeat Reward gives Event Currency, although in a smaller amount compared to Clear Rewards. Similar to Clear ones, Repeat Reward is also affected by Event Currency Boost Gain.

docs.title: Quick Battle
docs.text:
If you beat Normal / Challenge Battles for 5, 10, or 15 with all Clear Rewards, you will get access to the Quick Battle feature.

With this one, you can quickly spend your Event AP to get Repeat Rewards.

Image Guide

What order do I want to complete Battles?

If you can win every fight, then it does not matter.

Possible Routes (choose 1 up to your liking):

  • Normal Battles (1 - 15) → Challenge Battles (1 - 15) → Repeat Challenge Battle 15 until the last day
  • Challenge Battles (1 - 15) → Normal Battles (1 - 15) → Repeat Challenge Battle 15 until the last day
  • ...

docs.title: Auto-Play
docs.text:
You can automatically clear Normal and Challenge Stages using the Auto-play feature. This feature uses Auto Battle, as well as auto progression between stages.

The feature stops when you reach a set number of attempts used, you cancel manually, or your team dies, unable to complete a stage.

To enable the feature, press the Auto-Play button in the bottom right corner.

Image Guide

During the event, the first week is called the Preparation Period, during which you can only test your damage and teams without getting any rewards via Practice Battles.

The second week is called the Hunting Period, and it is the time you get rewards for engaging with the Boss.

docs.title: Fiend Hunter
docs.text:
Fiend Hunter is an activity revolving around defeating a Boss that becomes stronger with each level. Defeating the Boss successfully grants various rewards.

To access the game mode, press the Season Event logo, then click the corresponding button.

Image Guide

Fiend Hunter Menu

docs.title: Fiend Hunter Schedule
docs.text:
Fiend Hunter is Seasonal, biweekly content. Each Fiend Hunter season is separated into 2 phases, each lasting 1 week:

  • Preparation Period, during which you can do Practice battles and cannot obtain Rewards.
  • Hunting Period, during which you attack the Boss directly and gain Rewards based on your performance.
Event Schedule

The Fiend Hunter schedule completely aligns with Season Events; or, to be more precise, Fiend Hunter is a part of Season Events.

More about Season Events →

On the last day of the Hunting Period, a Settlement Period starts at 15:00 UTC, after which you can no longer challenge the Boss.

docs.title: Boss
docs.text:
Each Season you fight a different Boss. Each Boss occupies specific tiles of a 3x4 battlefield grid, similar to Regular Battles.

Example of the tiles that are occupied by the Boss

More about Grid System →

You can also check the tiles by inspecting the Boss info in the Fiend Hunter Menu.

Image Guide

docs.title: Boss Levels
docs.text:
Fiend Hunter Bosses have 25 initial Levels you can freely choose between in both Normal and Practice Battles. However, after defeating Level 25, you will face Level 26 — meaning the Boss, in theory, has infinitely many Difficulty Levels.

Each new Level is progressively harder thanks to scaling parameters such as HP and ATK / MATK.

docs.title: Boss Stats
docs.text:
Each Boss has its own predetermined Base Value, Initial Growth and Scale Growth parameters for HP and ATK or MATK. These three parameters determine the Boss's Health and Attack potential on each Difficulty Level.

Initial Growth is responsible for scaling immediately, starting from Level 2, while Scale Growth has a much greater impact at higher difficulties.

Additionally, Bosses have 3 stages, with State 2 and Stage 3 potentially carrying multiplier to adjust the parameters.

Stat Formula

\(\text{Value} = \text{round}\left[\text{Base} \cdot 1.1 \cdot \left(1 + (\text{Level}-1) \cdot \text{Rate} \cdot 0.01 \cdot \text{Level}^\text{Slope} \cdot \text{Stage Ratio}\right)\right]\)

  • \(\text{Base} \rightarrow \text{Base Value}\)
  • \(\text{Level} \rightarrow \text{Boss Level}\)
  • \(\text{Rate} \rightarrow \text{Initial Growth Parameter}\)
  • \(\text{Slope} \rightarrow \text{Scale Growth Parameter}\)
  • \(\text{Stage Ratio} \rightarrow \text{Level Related Multiplier}\)
Formula Explanations & Limitations
  • Rounding in the formula works as follows:
    • For HP, rounding down to 3 significant figures is applied.
    • For ATK and MATK, rounding to the nearest integer is applied instead, with 0.5 being rounded down.
  • Parameters do not change with level. However, boss has specific levels, after which a new Stage is applied. That can modify the final stat value, although recently (for at least 11 hunts) it has no impact.
Stats Data → Parameters Data →

docs.title: Boss Skills
docs.text:
All Bosses have two types of skills: Basic and Conditional Skills. Each Skill is "tied" to a specific body part of the Fiend Hunter Boss. You can check these Skills by inspecting the Boss in the Fiend Hunter Menu, just like the grid tiles.

Image Guide

  • Basic Skills are the ones that the Boss will definitely use during the fight.
    • The final Basic Skill always causes Instant Death, preventing you from playing for an extended turn period.
  • Conditional Skills are actions the Boss will use only if a particular condition is met.
    • Conditional Skills can only be triggered a fixed number of times per battle or a fixed number of times per team.
    • This type of Skill will be used instead of the next scheduled Basic Skill as soon as its condition is met, delaying the latter.

It is essential to understand the Skills to maximize your damage.

docs.title: Weak Points
docs.text:
Weak Points are specific body parts that may or may not be present.

Each Weak Point takes additional damage and is displayed as text reading WEAK along with a Damage Increase multiplier.

Weak Points Display

docs.title: Battle
docs.text:
For the Battle, you can deploy up to 3 teams with 5 Companions in each. Each team goes strictly in the set order (Team 1 → Team 2 → Team 3).

You are also free to choose any difficulty you want to face, up to Level 25.

Once the Battle starts and Team 1 perishes, Team 2 replaces it; this continues until every team has perished.

Fiend Hunter Battle

As mentioned earlier, the Boss has a set Skill pattern, which is displayed on the right side of the screen. You can also see the next Skill having the NEXT label. Skills are used from top to bottom, except for Conditional Skills.

Boss Skill Order

Combat Behavior

  • Boss Tiles cannot be knocked back or silenced.
  • Whenever a team dies from any source other than the Boss's final Basic Skill, the Boss Skill cycle continues, meaning the Boss will not reset their Skills.
    • This implies that teams should aim to survive until that final Basic Skill.
  • Characters cannot evade Boss hits. The only way to not get hit is to position your Companions correctly.

docs.title: Team Switch
docs.text:
You can quickly switch teams in Fiend Hunter. Switching only goes forward from Team 1 to Team 2 to Team 3, with no option to bring a previous team back.

Switching acts as an external Instant Death mechanic; therefore, it does not refresh the Boss's Skills.

This feature is overall rarely used, with the sole exception of saving time at high levels when you do not wish to climb higher but still want to claim your daily rewards.

Team Switch Warning Menu

docs.title: Damage Mechanic
docs.text:
Since you can challenge any Difficulty Level, it is possible that you won't deal enough damage to clear the entire run.

If this happens, you will automatically defeat all levels whose HP thresholds are lower than the damage you dealt. Your full damage score will then carry over and be applied to the next level.

Example

Assume the Boss named Baywatcher has 487M HP at Level 10, and 714M HP at Level 11.

If you challenge Level 15 but only manage to deal a total of 500M damage:

  • You will completely defeat Levels 1 through 10 (since 500M is greater than 487M).
  • You will deal that same 500M damage to Level 11, leaving it with 214M HP.

Any subsequent attempts to deal damage during the same day will have no impact, unless your new damage is higher than your previous record.

You can continue dealing damage to the Boss the following day, either by attacking manually or by using the Quick Battle feature.

Quick Battle

Quick Battle allows you to instantly apply your most serious recorded damage from the previous day. However, the system only saves this damage record for the highest level your damage actually reached, not the level you originally clicked on.

Using the example from above, even though you challenged Level 15 on Day 1, your damage only reached Level 11. Therefore, on Day 2, you will have Quick Battle unlocked only for Level 11.

Once you use Quick Battle, you will deal that same 500M damage and defeat Level 11.

However, you will no longer be able to Quick Battle Level 12 because your damage history never successfully reached it on Day 1, meaning you must challenge it manually.

Quick Battle Button Location

You can check how much daily damage you need to clear a specific Level using Souseha's Database or the Author's Fiend Hunter Sheets.

An Example of Fiend Hunter Damage Threshold Chart

docs.title: Break Season
docs.text:
Whenever a bug is found that heavily impacts rankings, a Break Season is introduced in place of a normal one.

During a Break Season, you will receive the rewards for Rank 1 (except the sticker and trophy) regardless of your personal ranking as long as you participated in Fiend Hunter at all.

You can spot a Break Season by checking in-game notifications or noticing the "Break Season" label within the Fiend Hunter menu itself.

Break Season

After some time, a Return Season will be introduced, featuring the same Boss.

...Even if this is a Break Season...

...you still should fight the Boss daily.

  • You still get all resources from Clear Rewards.
  • You also gain Event Currency that will not be obtainable during the Return Season, so you will want to clear out the Event Shop.

docs.title: Return Season
docs.text:
The Return Season is a rerun of the Break Season after the bug fix.

There is no fixed amount of time between the Break and Return Seasons. It also runs independently of the regular Fiend Hunter cycle. That means you should check Maintenance / Developer Notes for their schedule (if any).

Similar to the Break Season, the Return Season also has a label in the menu. Additionally, you can access the rerun season via the Home Screen.

Return Season & Access Guide

Since this is a rerun, no Preparation Period is given; instead, it starts directly from the Hunting Period and lasts for the entire duration of the current Fiend Hunter Boss's Preparation Period.

This ensures you do not have two Boss fights daily, but essentially forces you to attack different Bosses for three weeks straight (Hunting Period of the Boss №1 → Preparation Period of the Boss №2 & Hunting Period for the Return Season → Hunting Period of the Boss №2).

docs.title: Ban System
docs.text:
Since a Return Season happens later in the timeline, new costumes released in the interim could change the meta for that specific Boss.

To ensure fair play, a Ban System is introduced for Return Seasons.

Banned Costumes List During Return Season

This system forbids using Companions (or individual Costumes) for the Boss.

If all of a Companion's costumes are banned, they cannot be deployed for battle. Otherwise, if only one of their many Costumes is banned, you are allowed to deploy the Companion, but using the banned Costume will be prohibited.

docs.title: Rapport
docs.text:
Rapport is a system where you interact with specific Costumes via visual novel-style 'Diner Talks,' unlocking personal character stories and a global account buff that permanently boosts your team's Crit Rate.

TL;DR

  • You get 3 Talks a day total (not per Costume) to spend on owned Costumes; picking the preferred answer or gifting a Costume's favorite Drink gives the most EXP.
  • Leveling a Costume's Rapport unlocks its Personal Story and works toward the Rapport Buff, a permanent, global Crit Rate bonus (up to 50%, reached at 10 maxed Costumes).
  • A Costume's max Level Cap depends on its own upgrade progress: 10 on acquisition, 15 after Awakening, 20 after Potential Liberation — Awakening is mandatory for Level 15 even if Potential Liberation is already done.
  • Jump straight to the Rapport Answers & Gifts List if you're searching for one.

Rapport Menu

To access the Rapport Menu, either click on the Rapport button on the Home Screen or press the Talk button in the Companion tab for any Costume with an existing Rapport. Alternatively, use Glupy Diner to access the Rapport Feature as well.

Access via Home Screen

Access via Companion Tab

Access via Glupy Diner

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Each day you are given 3 Talks to interact with Costumes. You can interact with one costume only once, which essentially means you can interact with up to 3 Costumes per day and your attempts are reset at 15:00 UTC regardless of the number of attempts you had left beforehand.

You can only interact with and gift Costumes that you currently own.

Not every Costume has Rapport yet — whether a given Costume gets one is decided individually by the developers. Newly added Costumes will probably have it, while old ones will slowly get their own.

Interaction happens in the form of Talks, which are short situations with two choices. One choice is considered "preferred" and gives more EXP, while the other is "standard" and therefore gives less EXP.

docs.title: Talks
docs.text:
Each Talk is a situation where you have to pick an answer.

Talk Image

  • If you use the "preferred" answer, you will receive 100 EXP.
  • If you use the "standard" answer, you will receive only 80 EXP.

There are a total of 15 Talks for each Costume, with each Talk being labeled as a Visit and shown in the Talk Archives. Pressing the Talk button always grants EXP: while any Visits remain unseen, it picks one of them at random; once all 15 have been seen, it repeats one instead, still for full EXP. After all 15 Visits are acquired for the first time, you additionally receive 100 Dias as a one-time reward.

The Talk Archives let you review any Visit you've already completed, with its "preferred" / "standard" answers displayed more clearly — this is for reference only and grants no EXP or other reward.

Answers Display in Archive

Upon obtaining the maximum level for the Costume, you can talk an infinite number of times without being limited by the daily 1-Costume restriction, even for Visits you've never seen before — letting you complete the Archive in a matter of minutes.

docs.title: Quick Talk
docs.text:
Quick Talk is a feature that allows you to skip the Talk but gain only 80 EXP, similar to a "standard" answer. It is available after completing 5 Talks for a given Costume and behaves like a normal Talk, reducing your daily attempts by 1 for each Quick Talk used.

docs.title: Gifts
docs.text:
There are a total of 7 Gifts. You can give them to Costumes to increase their EXP.

All Gifts are obtainable from Powder of Hope and Golden Thread Shops.

Each Costume prefers a specific Drink. Gifting this specific drink will grant 40 EXP, while gifting any other will grant 20 instead.

Special Drink is preferred by everyone and will give you 150 EXP upon gifting.

To fully upgrade the Costume's Rapport, you need 53 Gifts.

Better Strategy

Instead of gifting 53 Gifts, first have a single Talk with the best answer.

This way, the number of Gifts required is lowered to exactly 50, which makes it easier to progress with multiple Costumes at once (due to the purchase limit of 100 on any given Gift, except Special Drink).

List of Gifts
  • Creamy Milk
  • Cold Beer
  • Velvety Wine
  • Fragrant Whiskey
  • Warm Black Tea
  • Sweet Soda
  • Special Drink

Are Gifts worth buying? Where to buy from?

  • Early game, neither of the shops is good to purchase from.
  • Later, the Golden Thread Shop is okay to buy from, provided you have bought Unidupe, Sparks of Rampage, Tears of Goddess and probably Draw Tickets. This holds until you max your Crit Rate bonus.
  • After you obtain the maximum Crit Rate bonus, Gifts value drops almost to zero, therefore, there is no reason to buy from either shop anymore.

docs.title: Costume Progression
docs.text:
Each Costume has its own EXP. By using Talks or Gifts on a specific Costume, you gain EXP. Once a specific amount of EXP is obtained, the Costume's level increases.

Each Costume has a separate Level Cap that limits the maximum level you can achieve for this costume. Level Cap depends on the Costume / Character upgrade progress.

  • Costume Acquired — Level 10
  • Character Awakening Complete — Level 15

Important Detail

You cannot progress further if you have Potential Liberation completed but no Awakening — you must have Awakening to get to Level 15.

This heavily impacts Support characters, who generally do not prioritize or benefit from Awakening as much as your DPS units.

Once you obtain Levels 10, 15, and 20, you obtain a special Reward. For Level 10, it is a collection item related to the Costume, while for Levels 15 and 20, the rewards are stickers instead.

docs.title: Story
docs.text:
Personal Stories allow players to experience exclusive, visual-novel-style lore chapters centered around the specific Costume.

There are 6 episodes in total, which unlock sequentially as you hit the specific level milestones. You also need to read the previous episode to unlock the next one.

Episode Requirements

  • Episode 1 — Level 1
  • Episode 2 — Level 3
  • Episode 3 — Level 5
  • Episode 4 — Level 7
  • Episode 5 — Level 9
  • Episode 6 — Level 10

Reading a Story episode does not grant Rapport EXP — it only rewards Dias, as detailed below.

Whenever the Season Event revolves around a specific Costume, their Story is unlocked for free for the duration of the Event regardless of the Costume's presence in your account, additionally giving Event Currency on top of 80 Dias for each episode by default. When the Season Event ends, the Story gets locked once again until you meet the requirements to read it like any other Costume's Story. It will be considered read after you re-unlock it.

docs.title: Rapport Buff
docs.text:
The Rapport Buff is a buff that increases Crit Rate and acts like a Collection Bonus.

This means the bonus is global, affects all permanent Companions, and cannot be reduced via Pressure Effects.

It has a maximum value of 50% and is obtained via completing Missions. Each mission gives 2%.

Rapport Buff Missions

Missions List

  • Reach Rapport Level 10 for [Costume]
  • Reach Rapport Level 20 for [Costume]
  • Reach Rapport Level 10 for 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 Character(s)
  • Reach Rapport Level 15 for 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 Character(s)
  • Reach Rapport Level 20 for 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 Character(s)

In-Game Text Clarification

The game's mission text uses the word "Characters", but the system tracks "Costumes" instead. It is a bad translation that can be confusing when the Rapport system adds more Costumes.

It takes 10 Costumes with Rapport Level 20 to obtain the maximum Rapport Buff.

Taros Tactical Manual is seasonal content featuring a grid of battles varying from 3 x 3 (9 battles) to 5 x 5 (25 battles). In each battle, you are given a fixed set of characters to win the battle.

Each season lasts for 28 days, giving you nearly a month to clear at most 25 short stages. After the season ends, the board and missions reset.

Each battle has a set difficulty: Easy, Normal, or Hard. They roughly reflect the fight's difficulty and grant different amounts of Gold per clear.

What upgrades do I buy with Obsidian?

Prioritize Refresh Attempts Up, Starting SP Up, followed by Discount Probability Up and ATK/MATK, depending on the team you usually run. The rest is optional and/or not needed.

Image of Upgrade Menu

At the start of your run, you have to draft a team. To do that, you need to pick 1 of 4 offered costumes for each slot. If you do not like the choice and have rerolls available, you can refresh the offered costumes.

Image of Normal Selection screen

As for the fifth pick, you're allowed to take almost every costume from the game as Wildcard Selection, except collab characters you do not own.

Image of Wildcard Selection screen

How to properly pick your Wildcard

  • First, you need to understand what type of team you gathered. If you picked a full Magical damage type of team, there is very little sense to switch to Physical type.
  • Second, you need to balance the team. If you picked good supports, try to consider picking DPS and vice versa.There may be rare cases where you get both supports and DPS in the first 4 picks. Then you can decide to bring in a Utility costume or add extra Support/DPS.

Some rules about costumes

  1. Owned costumes in your account copy their dupes count (+0 ~ +5), Potential Liberation, and Engraving & Awakening.
  2. Costumes DO NOT copy their gear equipped.
  3. Brown Dust II Exclusive costumes can appear in both Normal and Wildcard Selections. As mentioned earlier, collab costumes cannot appear/be chosen unless you own them.

  4. In the following Normal Selections,

    • The first 2 choices for costumes are from your already owned characters, unless you obtained all possible costumes for characters(for example, having Angel of Destruction Teresse can give you Beachside Angel or Medical Club costumes in the first two slots).
    • The last 2 choices are always new (for example, you will never see Teresse from those, as soon as you obtain any of her costumes).

    That means it can be worth obtaining a different costume of the desired character to have a chance to obtain the needed costume sooner.

During your climb, you need to choose the path which can consist of the following activities:

Name Icon Description Battle Just a plain battle. As a reward, you receive Lost Silver and Costume Selection. Elite Battle More difficult battle compared to the one above. Often involves some mini-bosses. As a reward, you receive Lost Silver (more compared to Normal Battles) and Artifact Selection Boss Battle Necessary to fight each 10th floor, usually the hardest ones. As a reward, you receive Lost Silver (more compared to both Elite and Normal Battles) and high-grade Artifact Selection, as well as Refresh Attempt. Artifact Artifact Selection Event It offers you ways to obtain Lost Silver and various Artifacts, but with possible drawbacks. Shop Shop is a place to buy new artifacts, purchase or upgrade owned costumes, and heal your characters using Lost Silver. Always available on floors 11 and 21.

Interest System

On each new floor, you receive 5% of your current Lost Silver as interest. Do keep it in mind when choosing your path.

RNG Manipulation in ToS

In Tower of Salvation, RNG is fixed. That means you cannot restart the battle with the same setup to crit in case you did not. However, to somehow change RNG, you can change DPS order, or inflict some extra damage such as knockback or basic attack from other characters.

Artifact System

Artifacts are items mostly giving buffs and either providing offensive or defensive capabilities.

  • There are 4 artifact rarities total: N (Common), R (Rare), SR (Super Rare), UR (Ultra Rare).
  • They can be acquired as a reward from Elite Battles, Artifacts activity, Events, or via purchasing in a Shop.
  • Some artifacts of low rarity can be combined to make one of better rarity, usually better compared to components. These artifacts will have a icon on the top left corner of the artifact card.It is safe to click this icon to check the recipe for combining.
    • To actually combine artifacts, head to the Sort tab and press the third tab on the left.
    Image Guide

  • You cannot have artifact duplicates; however, after combining, it is possible to obtain component ones back naturally.
  • Artifact (de)buffs amount IS NOT counted towards (de)buff-dependent costumes such as New Hire Nebris or Onsen Swordfighter Blade. All (de)buffs for increasing the damage must come from other costumes, not artifacts.
  • It is important to read artifact abilities and understand what type of build you want to run.
  • You should be aware of combining artifacts, thus, in some cases, picking Magic-related artifacts when you run Physical team may have sense.

Event System

  • Events offer you a few choices, from 2 to 4. You have the ability to read about all of them and make a decision based on your needs.
  • Some choices have a chance of success. If you fail, a negative effect is usually displayed before it takes place.
  • Some artifacts increase the success chance for events.
  • For some events, it is just possible to skip the event completely ("Leave the room").
  • You can check all possible events here.

Shop System

Each shop offers you:

  • 5 Artifacts of different rarities (usually, a higher chance of better ones the further you go).
    • Each artifact has a fixed price, and it does not depend on difficulty or floor you're on.
  • 4 Costumes of characters you own (whenever it is possible).
    • If it's not (you own all costumes for all but 3 or fewer characters), new character costumes will be offered instead.
  • 4 Costumes of characters you DO NOT own.
  • Ability to upgrade dupe of owned costumes (1000 per dupe of any character)
  • Ability to heal & revive your characters
  • Ability to refresh shop
    • It has a base price of 1,000 Lost Silver and increases each time you do it in the same shop.

There is also a thing called a discount. It works for Artifacts and Costumes only, offering 50% off for some options.

  • Discount chance depends on difficulty.
  • There are upgrades and artifacts capable of increasing the chance.

Crystal Battle

If you complete Floor 30 on Difficulty 10, an extra Floor, 31, will be unlocked. It serves as a decisive factor for the leaderboard

  • You have 5 attack turns to deal as much damage to the Crystal in a 3x3 grid as possible.
  • Crystal takes no actions, but for the battle you can use survived characters after Floor 30 only.
  • Since the leaderboard doesn't give any necessary benefit, there is no point in chasing maximum damage. Focus on completing Tower instead.

Important Feature You Should REALLY Know

During the battles, you can replace characters for 2 SP each. The replaced character will not have cooldowns on any of the costumesThat means, you can refresh a character's skills for 4 SP.Do keep in mind that it also removes all buffs applied before, so the best usage of this feature goes to utility/support characters.

So, I've read this all, but who to use?

It is really up to you. There are a few common possible tactics you can run.

  1. High Chain team, which utilizes high hit count characters and revolves around chain mechanics.
  2. Low Chain team, which utilizes the complete opposite and tries to be as low on chains as possible.

Both options are viable, as well as different Damage type you pick.This game mode is really good to understand the basics of the battles, so do not hesitate to experiment yourself.

docs.title: Golden Colosseum
docs.text:
Golden Colosseum is a weekly seasonal PvP content.

TL;DR

  • A Golden Colosseum season lasts one week, concluding with a brief Settlement period.
  • Golden Colosseum does not use Gear. Only Costumes upgrade levels (+5), Potential Liberation, Awakening, and Bursts matter.
  • Completing missions and ranking up rewards Aurum Coins, which can be spent in the Golden Colosseum Shop.

Golden Colosseum Main Menu

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
The Golden Colosseum is unlocked upon clearing all Pagan Tower (Story Pack 6) Main Quests.

To fight, you set up a team and Blessings tailored to the active season's Rules. While core combat mechanics remain stable across most seasons, specific parameters (like grid size, unit limits, and bans) rotate regularly.

Similarly to Mirror Wars, the battles are automatic and do not require an active input from a player.

Winning against the opponent grants Points, and losing decreases Points, correspondingly. Unlike the Mirror Wars, though, losing in Defense does not affect your points; only your offense matters.

Repeat Battle

To save your time, you can use Repeat Battle feature. It will automatically start the battles and skip them after first Costume's Action until the set number of attempts is exhausted.

To activate it, press Repeat Battle at the bottom right corner of the Golden Colosseum Menu.

Image Guide

docs.title: Team
docs.text:
The team consists of Costumes, not Characters. You set up one team for both offense and defense, as well as for going first or second.

Each Costume is separate, which means you can put multiple Costumes of the same Character. Additionally, each Costume is affected by its own Costume bond, Awakening, Character Level, and Costume Upgrade level. The only thing Costumes are not affected by is Gear.

To set the team, press the Formation button, then Replace, pick the needed Costume, and, finally, place it on the field and save the changes.

Image Guide

Additionally, in the Formation tab, you can freely change the order of your Costumes, similar to the regular battles.

docs.title: Blessings
docs.text:
Blessings are effects that impact you or your enemy. They are separated into three categories: Offense, Defense, and Utility.

To access the Blessings menu, press the Formation button followed by Settings on the right.

Image Guide

Blessings Menu

Each Blessing costs a specific amount of Blessing Points, based on how impactful the Blessing is. You can equip a limited number of Blessings, dictated by the total Blessing Points available. You also have to make two separate Blessing builds for going First or Second, with going second granting extra points to compensate for turn order.

To check each Blessing, refer to the Blessing Menu mentioned above. Alternatively, check Souseha's Database.

What Blessings to choose?

It comes down to the used team and the strategy. Check the Guide section below.

If you want to use Blessings of the other person but have only a list for going first or second, you can usually adjust it by picking higher/lower potency Blessings for more/less points.

For example, if the person has Curse of Limits I in their "going first" lineup, you can try picking both Curse of Limits I and Curse of Limits II for when you go second.

Blessing Order

Blessing order matters. They activate in order from the top to the bottom. That means, using Grace before Barrier of Life will provide more Energy Guard compared to using Barrier of Life before Grace.

docs.text:

docs.title: "Consistent" Rules
docs.text:
While parameters labeled as (Consistent) can technically be altered by developers in future seasons, they have remained stable defaults throughout 34 seasons:

  • Weekly Entry: You are given 100 base attempts per week. You can purchase up to 3 refills (100 attempts each) for 10 Dia per refill, capping out at 400 attempts for 30 Dia total per season.
  • Initiative: You cannot choose whether you go first or second; initiative is decided randomly at the start of battle.
  • Action Flow: Units alternate turns individually based on placement order.(Player Costume 1 → Enemy Costume 1 → Player Costume 2 → Enemy Costume 2...) (if you go first).
    • If the Enemy Costume 1 dies from Player Costume 1, Enemy Costume 2 takes its place, until all deployed enemy Costumes have acted.
    • If the enemy used all their Costumes in a given Turn, but you still have multiple unused Costumes, they will do their actions without the enemy using skills once again.
  • Cooldowns: Costumes have no Cooldowns between Turns.
  • SP Costs: SP is set to ∞ (ignored/bypassed), meaning skills do not cost SP to cast. However, available SP for scaling mechanics (e.g., Olivier) is treated as baseline 0.
  • Starting Points: You start with 1000 Ranking points.
  • Death Time Turn: At Turn 5, combat enters Death Time. Unlike standard game modes where skills remain active during Death Time, skills in Golden Colosseum are disabled completely, forcing units to use basic attacks alongside the ramping Death Time stat buffs/debuffs.

docs.text:

Missions Availability

However, you still can claim rewards during the Settlement Period, given you satisfied the conditions beforehand.

This is helpful if you complete your battles right before the deadline or forget to claim your rewards before settlement begins.

docs.title: Ranking
docs.text:
Similarly to the Mirror Wars, there are 29 Rankings. Reaching a specific Rank awards you with a different amount of Aurum Coins at the end of the Season.

The Season lasts for a week with a Settlement Period that starts at 15:00 UTC on the last day. It happens on Wednesday (UTC), the last day of the game week. During the Settlement Period, you cannot perform any Attacks, so be sure to use your Attempts before the period.

Golden Colosseum ranks players strictly by relative percentile brackets across the active player base. At the end of the season, all active players are sorted by their final Rating Points and divided into percentage cutoffs (e.g., Top 1%, Top 5%, Top 10%, etc.).

Understanding Game Wording

The game UI uses inverted wording for the ranking system. Here are some examples of how to translate the brackets:

  • Within the Top 0.1%: You performed better than at least 99.9% of players.
  • Above Top 10% - Below Top 12.5%: You performed worse than 10% of players but still better than 87.5%. In other words, you are within the Top 10% — 12.5% bracket of players.

docs.title: The Soul Wager
docs.text:
The Soul Wager is an Auto Battler Inventory Management Content Pack. In it, your goal is to clear a set number of Boards (each consisting of several stages) within a limited number of attempts within the same Board.

The Soul Wager Screen

docs.title: Unlock Requirements
docs.text: The Soul Wager is unlocked upon clearing all Edge of Dimension Main Quests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Soul Wager is seasonal content, with each season lasting 8 weeks. During the season, you have unlimited attempts to clear all Boards, with each containing a fixed number of Phases (battles). To complete the Board, you must complete all Phases.

To do that, you must purchase Tiles, Units and Gear from the Soul Wager in-battle Shop, place them on the Main Field, and start the automated battle.

For any Victory or Defeat, you receive Soul Tokens to continue your run (10 for a loss and 16 for a victory).

If you are defeated, the Battle Shop refreshes and the reroll counter resets, giving you a clean slate of options to try on your next attempt. However, if you lose all 5 of your Attempts (Defeats), the current Board completely resets, sending you back to Phase 1.

If you complete the Board, you get Alea Chips as shop currency to purchase resources for your general progression.

On the last day of the Season, a Settlement Period starts at 15:00 UTC, after which you can no longer participate in the Soul Wager.

docs.title: Field
docs.text:
The Phase Formation screen consists of three sections: Storage, Main Field, and Shop.

Formation Screen layout

docs.title: Main Field
docs.text:
The Main Field is a 7 x 7 field where you place your Tiles, Units, and Gear.

Each tile varies in size, ranging from 1 x 1 (1 square) to 2 x 2 or 1 x 4 (4 squares).

Units are placed on top of these tiles. Each unit has a unique footprint, varying in size from 1 x 1 (1 square) to 3 x 4 with missing corners (8 tiles).

Rotation

You can rotate your Tiles and Units.

  • PC: Hold LMB and click RMB to rotate clockwise by 90°.
  • Phone / Tablet: Tap and hold with one finger, then tap with another to rotate clockwise by 90°.

Some deals may feature a reduced price.

docs.text:
The Storage section is a space where you can leave your purchased Board Pieces. They will not be used in battle, and there is no penalty for storing them.

Additionally, the Storage zone features a "gravity" system. Placing any stored piece on the left side of the storage panel automatically slides it flush against the right boundary, behaving like a sideways Tetris stack.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
The Codex is a place to learn more about Tiles, Units and Gear. To access it, press the corresponding icon on top of the screen before a run, or at the bottom of the screen during a run.

Image Guide

Codex View

docs.title: Tiles
docs.text:
There are a total of 5 different Tiles, each varying in shape, cost, and abilities. They are required to place Units on.

Tile Codex

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Units can only be placed on top of the Tiles. To deploy and use a unit, you must have unoccupied tile space available.

Each Unit has a distinct Grade and set of Tags. While a Unit's Grade determines its shop appearance rarity, its Tags briefly outline its gameplay role.

Tags List

There are a total of 8 Tags:

  • Close-Range Attack: This Character performs a close-range attack upon every cooldown reset.
  • Defending: Defending Characters have abilities that are triggered when the opponent attacks.
  • Support (Utility): Utility Characters grant Buffs to their allies.
  • Heal: Heal Characters have the ability to restore HP.
  • Curse: Curse Characters apply Debuffs to the opponent.
  • Long-Range Attack: This Character performs a long-range attack upon every cooldown reset.
  • Cleanse: Cleanse Characters remove Debuffs on yourself.
  • Remove: Remove Characters remove Buffs on the opponent.

Every attacking unit has a few key stats:

  • DMG — Damage per hit. It features its own value range, with a random value selected for each Action.
  • Stamina Cost — Stamina used per Action.
  • Accuracy Rate — The chance that an Action successfully deals damage to the enemy.
  • Cooldown — The interval between a Unit's Actions.

Unit Description Explanation

Certain units benefit from specific conditions tied to how you place their tiles on the grid. These requirements are indicated on their skill cards by the icon. These bonuses only trigger if the required tiles are actually placed on the battlefield grid.

For example, you cannot trigger Elise - Code Name O's enhanced restoration if her target tiles are rotated off the active board layout.

Image Explanation

Additionally, certain Units generate Buffs for the team or Debuffs for the enemy. You can learn more about them from Units' cards or check below.

Soul Wager Buffs

  • | Regeneration: For every stack, restores 1 HP every 2s.
  • | Overheat: For every stack, increases Action Speed by 2%.
  • | Lifesteal: For every stack, restores HP equal to close-range DMG dealt. Healing is capped at max stacks.
  • | Focus: For every stack, increases Accuracy Rate of all Characters by 5%.
  • | SP: Used to trigger certain effects. SP in and of itself does not have effects.
  • | Strength: For every stack, increases the DMG dealt by Attacking Characters by 1.
  • | Counter: For every stack, deals Counter DMG equal to DMG taken from close-range attacks. If DMG is higher than stack count, deals Counter DMG equal to stack count.

Soul Wager Debuffs

  • | Poison: For every stack, takes 1 DMG every 2s.
  • | Frost: For every stack, reduces Action Speed of all Characters by 2%
  • | Darkness: For every stack, reduces the Accuracy Rate of all Characters by 5%.
  • | Laceration: For every stack, increases the Stamina Cost of Attacking Characters by 2%.

Units Upgrading

You can upgrade Units, which will improve their Actions. Units can be upgraded to +5, similarly to the main game, with the exception that you cannot upgrade a Unit higher than their current rank in your main roster.

Each Upgrade level costs differently for each Unit.

docs.title: Battle
docs.text:
Pressing the "Battle" button in the bottom right corner begins the match.

Battle Screen

Combat is fully automated and continues until one side's total HP is reduced to 0. If both sides reach 0 HP simultaneously, the player is declared the winner.

During the battle, all Units on the field perform their actions based on their respective cooldowns. The only exceptions are Units that lack individual cooldowns, instead triggering off incoming enemy attacks, allied actions, specific conditional actions, or "Upon Battle Start" triggers (such as Seir - Demon's Daughter, Eclipse - Dream Bride, Refithea - Poolside Fairy, and Jayden - Beautiful Girl Devotee, respectively).

While grid placement matters for triggering team synergy bonuses, spatial positioning does not affect combat targeting. All deployed units strike the entire enemy field simultaneously, meaning you can place your DPS units on any tile or rotate the board layout without changing your team's total damage output.

When a unit performs an Action that requires Stamina, the cost specified on its Unit card is deducted from the team's shared Stamina pool. If the shared pool lacks enough Stamina to fund the action, the Unit cannot perform the move (displaying "Out of Stamina") and will enter its cooldown cycle once again.

More about Stamina

During the Preparation Phase, you can see the Stamina Cost on top. It is calculated as the sum of average Stamina usage across all Units and does not account for Stamina restoring Actions.

  • Very Low: 0.0 — 4.9 Stamina.
  • Low: 5.0 — 9.9 Stamina.
  • Medium: 10.0 — 14.9 Stamina.
  • High: 15.0 — 19.9 Stamina.
  • Very High: >20.0 Stamina.

docs.title: End Game
docs.text:
If a match takes longer than 20 seconds to conclude, the End Game mechanic activates. This mechanic inflicts damage over time (DoT) every second to both sides, based on the value displayed under the END GAME label.

The damage scales every 3 seconds upward according to the following logic:

  • Below 10 Damage: The value increases by a flat +1.
  • 10 Damage and Above: The value begins scaling by 11% every 3 seconds.
Exact Scaling Formula

In reality, the system runs an exponential 11% scaling curve in the background starting from second 1. To smooth the damage curve from the beginning, the system uses +1 increments instead.

Once the background exponential curve naturally surpasses 10, the game switches from the flat +1 floor to the true calculated curve. Because the background curve does not land exactly on 10 before its next iteration, subsequent values are derived from the underlying unrounded formula rather than exactly 10 x 1.11. All final ticking damage values are rounded up to the nearest integer.

\[ \text{Damage} = \left\lfloor\frac{\text{Current Battle Time}}{3}\right\rfloor - 6, \: 20 \le \text{Current Battle Time} \le 48 \\ \text{Damage} = \left\lceil 1.11^{\left\lfloor\frac{\text{Current Battle Time}}{3}\right\rfloor + 6}\right\rceil, \: \text{Current Battle Time} \ge 48 \]

docs.title: Fantasia Territory
docs.text:
Territory is a cozy management mode where players gather resources through farming, logging, and mining to build, landscape, and customize their own town while populating it with character residents.

TL;DR

  • This is a game mode that does not impact your game progress in any way. Think of it as an optional time killer.
  • To generate the currency, Local Points, you need to actively farm and sell the cooked dishes. Refer to the guide below for more information.
  • Start by heavily investing in Farming, while upgrading your Axe and Pickaxe to increase resource yields and unlock decorations.

It is located in Fantasia Square. To access it, walk down the staircase at the bottom of the Square.

Image Guide

docs.title: Activities
docs.text: There are three main activities you need to perform to progress in the Territory: Logging, Mining, and Farming. While Logging and Mining provide progression resources such as Rock or Lumber, Farming primarily provides Local Points.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Logging is done via the Logging Site. It is the main source of Wooden Branches, Lumber and Sturdy Lumber. To obtain them, you must chop down a tree using the Axe.

Each tree has 3 stages of growth, with a more grown version providing more resources and Logging EXP but taking longer to chop down.

Therefore, you should always chop down only fully grown trees to obtain the maximum amount of resources.

Different Growth Stages

Technical Details
  • The Logging Site is a 3x3 field, resulting in a maximum of 9 trees.
  • Whenever any tile is empty, the Logging Site will grow one Stage 1 tree in 60 seconds. Therefore, if you chop down all the trees, it will take 9 minutes to replenish them completely.
  • A tree needs 120 seconds to grow into Stage 2 and 180 seconds to grow into Stage 3; therefore, it takes 5 minutes to get a fully grown tree after it appears initially.
  • A tree's health determines how difficult it is to chop down, requiring a different number of hits depending on your progression.

docs.title: Mining
docs.text:
Mining is done via the Quarry. It is the main source of Rock, Copper Ore, Iron Ore, Silver Ore and Gold Ore. To obtain them, you must mine the clusters with a Pickaxe.

Ores have different chances to appear; however, unlike trees, they do not grow and can be mined immediately upon spawning.

Technical Details
  • Similar to the Logging site, the Quarry is a 3x3 field, resulting in a maximum of 9 clusters. The positioning isn't fixed in place; therefore, clusters are spawned randomly within the Quarry.
  • Whenever there are fewer than 9 ore clusters at any given moment, the Quarry will generate 1 cluster in 60 seconds. Therefore, if you mine all clusters, it will take 9 minutes to fill the Quarry again.

docs.title: Select Territory (Terrain)
docs.text:
During the intro, you can choose 1 of 6 Territory layouts: Plain Terrain, River Terrain 1, River Terrain 2, Coast Terrain, Beach Terrain I, and Beach Terrain II.

Your chosen terrain does not affect your progression.

You cannot place anything except Bridges on Water Tiles, which technically means that the Plain Terrain layout contains the most buildable tiles.

Terrain Selection

You can change the Terrain at any given point via Phone, but doing so will:

  • Destroy all structures you've built, with a material refund.
  • Destroy all crops, trees, and ores without a refund.
  • Remove all expansions, with a Local Points refund.

This essentially means that for refunding, you should not have any active crops growing and be ready to spend time rebuilding all buildings from scratch.

docs.title: Dishes
docs.text:
Dishes are the items you can create using a Cooking Pot. They can be consumed to obtain a temporary bonus or be sold for Local Points.

Each dish provides different bonuses, but all have a 10-minute duration. Consuming the same dish again extends the bonus duration, while bonuses from different dishes stack.

An Example

  • If you consume Virile Gnocchi, you will get +8 Logging Skill for 10 minutes.
  • If you consume two Virile Gnocchis, you will get +8 Logging Skill for 20 minutes instead.
  • If you consume Virile Gnocchi and Curvaceous Fried Rice, you will get +18 Logging Skill and +10 Mining Skill for 10 minutes instead.

docs.title: Cooking Guide
docs.text:
There are several strategies when it comes to gaining Local Points.

They can be roughly divided into Active (Early Game), More Passive (Late Game), and Lazy.

Active (Early Game)More Passive (Late Game)Lazy

The main income for the early game and active gameplay comes from Virile Gnocchi.

It is easy to mass-produce and is available immediately; however, this requires constantly playing the game, which is a significant downside on its own.

A more passive approach revolves around the Crop Bonus from dishes.

That involves three dishes:

  • Lingerie Cookie
  • Lustful Tart
  • Libido Soup

The idea relies on consuming these three dishes before harvesting fully grown ingredients for them, such as Pulse Saffron.

Therefore, you must always save 3 of each dish listed above and cycle their production to maximize the Crop Bonus.

Alternatively, you can grow Venus Cacao, Stamina Pepper, Lustful Grape, Sticky Melon and Pulse Saffron in a ratio of 3:3:3:3:88 (3 Venus Cacao, 3 Stamina Pepper, 3 Lustful Grape, 3 Sticky Melon and 88 Pulse Saffron placed at the same time).

If you have Helpers with high Farming Efficiency, you can manually grow Pulse Saffron only and let Helpers grow the rest of the necessary crops.

Honestly, cooking any food results in a net positive. Therefore, you can ignore all advice and grow whatever you want based on what best fits your login schedule.

Territory is not tied to the main gameplay; therefore, there is no reason to rush anything when it comes to this game mode.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tools are designed to improve resource-gathering efficiency.

There are 3 tools, each having 4 rarities: Stone, Copper, Silver, and Gold.

While Stone tools are given by default, you can upgrade them in the Forge. Each upgrade costs Materials and Local Points.

Technical Details
  • Pickaxe and Axe increase Mining and Logging Skills, as well as Lumber and Mineral bonuses respectively.
  • Sickle, on the other hand, increases Farming Skill and Simultaneous Harvesting Capacity — the amount of crops you can collect in one swing.

docs.text:
1. Axe and Pickaxe. Their upgrades increase the quantity of items obtained, similar to the Pub and Warehouse buildings.
  2. Sickle. It will help you grow rarer crops and collect more of them within one swing, which can be crucial during Late Game Cooking Strategy.

Axe / Pickaxe are slightly better due to the increased item drop that you can use as an additional income source from selling raw materials.
